original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Whole-tree source-impact inventory of the unsound bit-0/balanced word-census prune at the base commit. Every file with the faulty engine bytes, a cyclic_census definition or call, the #2691 native rule, the old L18/L20 receipts or a 20<=f(7) citation is classified against replacement evidence. A calibration binds the faulty hash to the 01021323 false prune on the complete n=4, L=8 simple domain.
scope_change_reason: The card's calibration, #2542 trace, small exhaustive domain and a six-file call-site inventory are already merged (#3096, #3821, #3215), as are independent corrected replays (#3005, #3333). #3215 states that its inventory is not a whole-repository dependency proof. This package takes that remaining obligation, which is the allowed 'one downstream dependency audit' variation. It repeats the calibration and the n=4, L=8 domain only to bind the faulty engine hash to the defect.
bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism. A whole-tree dependency boundary shows that no currently relied-upon f(7) exclusion uses the faulty rule, and it names the stale anchors, so no further census is needed to repair it.
stop_rule: Stop after a pinned whole-tree classification at the base commit, a hash-to-defect calibration and rejection controls. No seven-label census, no L22 work, no edits to frozen packages, no supplier or frontier change.
evidence: verify.py (default): 01021323 budgets (weight excess 0 within budget 5; bit-0 excess 8 against balanced budget 5 and actual budget 9); the faulty PR2542 engine bytes (SHA-256 82e4c407...) agree with an independent oracle on all 22 simple universal n=4, L=8 words without a budget and falsely prune exactly 6 with the balanced budget, while the weight-parity rule prunes 0; 26 pinned inventory files with quoted evidence and role invariants; 7 rejection controls. verify.py --rescan at base cef4b52: 90,399 files scanned, every trigger file (faulty bytes, cyclic_census, native nq&1/BUDGET rule, old L18/L20 receipts, 20<=f(7)) is under one of 21 classified prefixes, with 0 unclassified and 0 stale.
result: The bit-0/balanced pruning rule is disproved. No final bound is disproved. The retired word exclusions are #2542 L18, #2634 partial L20 and #2691 (10,10) L20; all three have merged replacement evidence (#2973, #3005, #3333, #3058 sections 1-2). The set-level packages #2773-#3023 are unaffected by the bit-0 error. #2773, #2870, #2911 and #2933 carry L18 universal=0 anchors from the unsound filter, and #2773-#3023 cite 20<=f(7). Those need reading notes, not revalidation. The replacement engines contain no faulty bytes, no cyclic_census call and no nq&1 grouping.

open_questions.question: Should frozen packages with historical L18 anchors (#2773 verify.py, #2870, #2911, #2933 receipts) carry a reading note or a successor entry point?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Their PASS output prints universal_words=0 from the unsound filter, which a reader can take for exclusion evidence.
open_questions.first_step: A maintainer decides between a central annotation index keyed by INVENTORY.json paths and successor entry points.
open_questions.blocked_by: Frozen-package policy; this is a maintainer decision.

open_questions.question: Can the single-engine L22 exclusions (#3818, #4221) get a second, separately written implementation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The f(7)=24 word line at L22 rests on one C engine; #3899 is auditing its union prune only on tiny domains.
open_questions.first_step: Extend #3005's census past its L<=20 gate on one small L22 split such as (11,7) and compare node-exactly with a capped union-engine run.
open_questions.blocked_by: #3005's length gate and unmeasured L22 throughput.

open_questions.question: Can the rescan detect phrase-level citations of the old exclusions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Citations without the receipts, the faulty bytes or the 20<=f(7) form are invisible to the syntactic scan.
open_questions.first_step: Add patterns such as 'length 18 excluded' and classify every new hit at a fixed base.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing structural; the false-positive rate is unmeasured.
